amv.title: iOS Engineer I → II
amv.summary: Four and a half years building physical-therapy software: two cognitive therapy apps used in clinics, then an AI exercise-guidance app I built alone from an empty repository.

products.name: AMV ConnEx
products.pitch: A patient app for home exercise programs. The camera watches you move and tells you, in real time, how well you are doing the exercise your clinician prescribed.
points: Took the app from first commit to App Store launch in about 13 months, owning architecture and every release.

Embedded a Unity computer-vision module (MediaPipe) in a native app for on-device joint tracking: an Objective-C++ bridge loads UnityFramework at runtime, Swift sends it JSON commands, and results come back as movement summaries that upload through a background queue.
Built HIPAA-compliant clinician–patient messaging with SwiftData offline sync, a home-screen widget for the prescription schedule, session reminders and clinician booking.
Wrote the shared Swift package both company apps depend on (networking, auth, models, theming, components), and a networking layer that cut API boilerplate by roughly 80%.
Moved the codebase to MVVM with coordinators and dependency injection, then through the Swift 6 strict-concurrency migration.

products.name: Cog PT & Cog PT Companion
products.pitch: Cognitive therapy for physical-therapy patients. Clinicians run assessments and prescribe training in Cog PT; patients do the work at home in the Companion app.
points: Used in 22 clinics in Texas. Cog PT was distributed privately through Apple Business Manager; the Companion app shipped 10 App Store releases.
Resolved 20+ production crashes and 45+ bugs. Cog PT then ran 116 consecutive days without a crash, and the Companion went 161 days without a bug report.
Wrote 70+ automated tests (XCTest and XCUITest) that supported the audit trail for a pre-FDA Software-as-a-Medical-Device submission.
Built cognitive task screens, the prescription flow, dual-tasking (an exercise and a cognitive task at once, with heart rate from a Bluetooth sensor) and clinician charts.
Also worked on the Firebase backend: security rules, clinic-access claims and Cloud Functions.
facts: ~120K lines of Swift across both apps

amv.also: I also made UI changes to 94FEETOFGAME, a basketball training app from the same venture group, during 2022. Someone else was its main developer.

process.title: Agents merge. Humans release.
process.intro: Since May 2026 I have built two apps by directing Claude Code and Cursor instead of typing most of the code myself. What makes that work is the harness around the agent, which I designed and keep tightening.

steps.name: Rules
steps.text: Scoped rule files tell the agent how this codebase works: architecture boundaries, naming, what never to touch.

steps.name: Work
steps.text: Each task runs in its own git worktree and simulator, so several agents can work at once without colliding.

steps.name: Gate
steps.text: A hook runs the unit tests when the agent tries to stop. Red tests send it back to work. On Silver Screen that is 940+ tests.

steps.name: Proof
steps.text: UI changes need simulator screenshots in the pull request. CI runs API, Postgres, XCUITest and Compose UI tests.

steps.name: Review
steps.text: Every pull request gets a code review pass before it merges. Agents may merge their own reviewed work.

steps.name: Release
steps.text: Only I can tag a release. A guard hook blocks agents from tagging or touching production, and the App Store phased rollout halts itself if the Sentry crash-free rate drops.

process.meta: This site works the same way. A scheduled job watches my app repositories for new release tags, reads what changed, and opens a pull request here only when a build changes something a visitor would care about.
